author: opencode-worker-3
text: Round 2 findings: (a) tx_queue RETRY hypothesis DISPROVEN — lora_l2_tx is synchronous push-then-pop (lora_l2_tx.c:255-279), no re-send path exists for built frames. (b) The loopback rx_queue is re-inited (k_msgq_init in lora_loopback_init, 'initialized' logged in the failing window), so stale frames cannot survive there either. (c) Remaining candidates for the (142, seq0/seq1) re-delivery: [1] init_link_ctx_locked (and its replay_table_init) SKIPPED in the queue_stats enable because link_ctx_initialized was still 1 — i.e. the disable path did not clear it before enable ran (verify: log link_ctx_initialized at enable entry, and whether the table-generation changes); [2] the rejected frames are IPv6 NDP NS retransmits (1s cadence matches .350->1.250) whose FIRST deliveries committed silently and whose seq values collided with pre-reset commits — which would mean tx_seq did NOT advance as expected after reprovision (checkpoint absent in that build: last round's link_ctx.c WAS on heft during capture, so checkpoint was active — verify restored_seq actually reached ctx->tx_seq). NEXT DIAGNOSTIC (single build): add TX-side DIAG at lichen_link_next_tx (log epoch/seq per allocation) plus a one-line log at init_link_ctx_locked entry; run the suite; the combined TX/RX picture will pin whether seq0/1 are re-TX or re-delivery. DIAG log from this round (kept in git history of this comment): commit_replay failures epoch=142 seq=0 and seq=1, pk 41b9e055...
